dhp256:1: Not therefore is a man called a justice because he decides a cause arbitrarily;
dhp256:3: Nay rather is it he that inquires into both right and wrong, he that is wise.
dhp257:1: He that leads others without violence, justly and righteously,
dhp257:3: He that is protected of the Law, he that is intelligent, he alone is properly called a justice.
dhp258:1: Not therefore is a man called wise for his much speaking;
dhp258:3: He that is patient, free from hatred, free from fear, he alone is called wise.
dhp259:1: Not therefore is a man versed in the Law for his much speaking.
dhp259:3: But he that hears ever so little, and evidences his perception of the Law by his acts,
dhp259:5: He is indeed versed in the Law, for he fails not to heed the Law.
dhp260:1: Not therefore is a man an Elder because his head is gray;
dhp260:3: Though he be ripe in years, yet he is called ‘Old-in-vain.’
dhp261:1: That man in whom dwell truth, righteousness, non-injury, temperance, and self-control,
dhp261:3: He that has rid himself of his faults and is steadfast, that man is truly called an Elder.
dhp262:1: Not through eloquence or beauty of complexion
dhp262:3: Is a man accomplished, if at the same time he be envious, niggardly, deceitful.
dhp263:1: But he that has cut off and uprooted and removed all these faults,
dhp263:3: He that has rid himself of hatred, he that is intelligent, such a man is rightly called accomplished.
dhp264:1: No tonsure can make a monk of a man who is undisciplined, who speaks falsehood;
dhp264:3: If a man be affected with desire and cupidity, how can he be a monk?
dhp265:1: But he that overcomes sins both small and great, wholly and entirely,
dhp265:3: He is rightly called, from victory over sins, a monk.
dhp266:1: Not therefore is a man a monk because he receives alms from others.
dhp266:3: He that adopts the religion, forms and all, is not on that account a monk.
dhp267:1: Whoever in this world casts out both merit and demerit, lives a life of chastity,
dhp267:3: Walks wisely through the world, he is a monk indeed.
dhp268:1: Not because of silence is a man a sage, if he be foolish and ignorant.
dhp268:3: But the wise man who takes to himself truth, even as one grasps a pair of scales,
dhp269:1: And rejects those things that are evil, such a man is a sage, and for this reason is a sage.
dhp269:3: He that understands both worlds is therefore called a sage.
dhp270:1: Not therefore is a man Noble because he injures living beings;
dhp270:3: A Noble is so called because he never injures living beings.
dhp271:1: Not merely because of religious practices, nor yet because of much learning,
dhp271:3: Neither because of attainment of Tranquillity, nor because of living solitary and remote,
dhp272:1: Win I the Bliss of Release, incapable of attainment by worldlings.
dhp272:3: Monk, rest not content until thou hast attained Destruction of the Depravities.
